hypothesis: tornado.escape.xhtml_escape does not escape the single quote character ('), so it is unsafe for use in single-quoted HTML attributes.
trigger: Call tornado.escape.xhtml_escape("'") and check whether the result contains the escaped entity ''' or '''.
potential_failure: The function returns the raw single quote unchanged, allowing attribute injection when the escaped value is placed inside a single-quoted HTML attribute.

oracle.expected_behavior: tornado.escape.xhtml_escape("'") should return a string that does not contain a literal single quote, i.e. it should be ''' or '''.
oracle.target_evidence: The docstring of tornado.escape.xhtml_escape states: 'A subset of the XHTML specification. This function only escapes the characters that are necessary for XHTML, which are &, <, >, ", and \'.' The function is intended for escaping text inserted into HTML, including attributes. The ordinary test tornado/test/escape_test.py::test_xhtml_escape checks escaping of &, <, >, and ", but does not test the single quote. The implementation in tornado/escape.py uses a translation table that maps only those four characters.
